reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive disaccharidase defect caused by SI variants that impair the brush-border sucrase-isomaltase enzyme
Symptoms typically appear when sucrose and starch are introduced, with watery osmotic diarrhoea, bloating, abdominal pain and failure to thrive
The osmotic diarrhoea abates during fasting or a sucrose-free diet, distinguishing it from secretory diarrhoeas
Unabsorbed sugars are fermented by colonic bacteria, giving acidic, frothy stool with a low stool pH and reducing substances
Diagnosis is supported by low sucrase activity on duodenal disaccharidase assay of biopsy tissue and by sucrose or starch breath testing
Management is dietary restriction of sucrose and starch, with enzyme substitution therapy as an adjunct to broaden dietary tolerance
Symptoms often become milder with age as diet and intestinal capacity adjust
reference.pathophysiology: Congenital sucrase-isomaltase deficiency is an osmotic malabsorption disorder of the small-intestinal brush border. Variants in SI reduce or abolish the activity of the sucrase-isomaltase complex, which normally hydrolyses sucrose and the alpha-1,6 and some alpha-1,4 bonds of starch-derived oligosaccharides. Undigested disaccharides and oligosaccharides remain in the lumen, drawing water osmotically into the bowel and passing to the colon where bacterial fermentation produces gas and short-chain acids. This yields acidic, watery, gassy diarrhoea that resolves when the offending carbohydrates are withheld.
additionalDifferentials: Coeliac disease with secondary disaccharidase deficiency
Functional gastrointestinal disorders and irritable bowel syndrome
Cow's milk protein or other food intolerances
additionalInvestigations: Duodenal biopsy with disaccharidase enzyme assay showing reduced sucrase activity
Sucrose or starch hydrogen/methane breath testing
Stool pH and reducing substances after a carbohydrate challenge
Molecular genetic testing for SI variants
Trial of sucrose and starch elimination with symptom monitoring
redFlags: Significant dehydration during acute diarrhoeal episodes in infants
Failure to thrive from chronic carbohydrate malabsorption
Persistent symptoms despite dietary measures suggesting an alternative or additional diagnosis
Onset of new alarm features prompting evaluation for coeliac or other mucosal disease
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is excellent with appropriate dietary management, and many patients tolerate increasing amounts of sucrose and starch with age. Growth and quality of life are normal once symptoms are controlled.
pitfalls: Attributing chronic osmotic diarrhoea to a functional disorder and not testing disaccharidase activity
Overlooking hidden sucrose and starch in processed foods and medicines during dietary restriction
Missing coeliac disease, which can cause a secondary reduction in disaccharidase activity
Assuming a negative single breath test excludes the condition without correlating with biopsy or genetics
references: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
